notes: EXHAUSTIVE pass: 4870 entities over 375 source files (263 plugin/scripts + 112 packages/*/src), yielding 135 corrected non-mirror byte-identical cross-file clusters + 213 same-symbol clusters = 348 candidates. All 16 shards returned; 129 clusters were source-verified by the shard agents and the remaining 46 thin (10-59b) clusters were verified by the final shard, so every cluster in the dispatched set was read at source. THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS were applied to my own inventory, and two were caught BY the shard agents rather than by me: (1) the first digest blanked string literals, so text-emitting usage() functions falsely clustered - recomputed with literals kept, removing 15+ false clusters; (2) arrow-const bodies were captured to the first semicolon even when nested, producing one spurious 2-byte cluster spanning 32 symbols and a false positive on fail()-style factories; (3) as yet uncorrected in the cluster list - for declarations with an object-literal return type the extractor sometimes keyed on the TYPE LITERAL rather than the body, producing roughly 10 further spurious clusters whose members share only a shape such as { ok: boolean; reason: string | null }. Every finding reported here was confirmed by a shard reading the real bodies and the known artifacts are excluded, but the inventory counts above should be read as a screen, not a measurement. The probe spec named identity-replication-check.ts as the PRIMARY FALLBACK instrument and it cannot run: it exits 1 with ENOENT on three git-tracked dangling symlinks (git-lens-l-d/g/s star, targets deleted by commit 9547d48eb), so the inventory was built with a purpose-written node extractor and that instrument failure is itself reported as a finding. COVERAGE: only 6 of the 213 same-symbol clusters were dispatched as clusters; that class was otherwise measured directly by the lead for the flag-reader, escape, comment-masking, sha256, sleep, selftest, walker and intra-file families. Runtime behaviour was reproduced end-to-end for exactly one finding - the stale direct-entry guard, where node plugin/scripts/dist/external-dogfooding-check.js --selftest prints drivable-workspace-check selftest lines while the same script run from source prints its own - and is inferred from source reading elsewhere, notably the live stripHeadings divergence in task list --search.

>=18 call sites use SEVEN distinct fence-detection grammars (CRLF-tolerant fm+body, CRLF fm-only, LF-only fm+body, LF-only fm-only, startsWith+indexOf, startsWith+/^---$/m, presence-only); I executed the regexes: a CRLF task file MATCHES all mechanism-side grammars and NO-MATCHES both product-side grammars, where grammar 3 THROWS and grammar 4 silently returns null.

Same process.kill(pid,0) probe, opposite error handling: driver-runtime's bare catch returns false so EPERM reads DEAD, while server-state/server-partial-stop return err.code==='EPERM' i.e. ALIVE; observable on this host (kill(1,0) raises EPERM). driver-runtime also coerces via Number() so the string '1' readPidFile returns is probed, whereas server-state's Number.isInteger('1') is false and returns DEAD without probing.

Four strategies under four names; the realpath-both-sides fix landed in config-wiring-check/drivable-workspace-check/concurrent-batch-scheduler but the naive form survives in 6+ files that omit realpathSync — under the experiments mirror symlink (and inside an esbuild bundle) the guard returns false and main() silently never runs, exit 0 with zero output, indistinguishable from a clean pass.

driver-runtime derives boot time from /proc/uptime plus a self-derived tick rate and its own comment rejects the other approach; observation uses /proc/stat btime (integer seconds) with a HARDCODED 100 — the hard-rule-4-corollary-2 pattern where a literal is correct only on the machine it was written for, giving readings up to ~1s apart here and proportionally wrong on any host with USER_HZ!=100.

write-json-atomic.ts's header claims it is 'the single atomic JSON-file write for EVERY state writer' and names the six it fixed, but at least three state writers still call fs.writeFileSync in place with no tmp/rename/fsync — meta-driver writes .quay/meta-driver-state.json whose reader maps an unparseable file to {digest:null}='never judged' (hard rule 3b), pool-quality-judge writes .quay/pool-quality-judge-state.json read back cross-process, driver-anchor rewrites .quay/anchor.json every reconcile pass.

At least 8 independent tmp-then-rename implementations coexist and they disagree on the exact property write-json-atomic's header gives as its reason to exist: the canonical uses ${p}.tmp-<pid>-<rand> while doc-check-cache and worker-driver's writeScopedGateCache use a BARE ${file}.tmp and ready-pool-check/driver-runtime use .tmp-<pid> — and .quay/doc-check-cache.json and .quay/scoped-gate-cache.json are each written by concurrent per-task worker-driver processes.

Three 0-byte files named in exactly the ${p}.tmp-<pid>-<hex> scheme sit in .quay/ on disk, proving a process died between tmp-create and rename; grep for unlink/rmSync/cleanup/readdir over 'tmp-' in plugin/scripts returns zero hits, so no writer or sweeper ever removes an orphan tmp and they accumulate permanently.

7 definitions across 5 distinct implementations; read failure returns silent [] in 6 of 7 (freshness throws instead) and line-parse failure is silently skipped in ALL 7 with none counting skipped lines, so 0 is a single value covering {absent, empty, every line corrupt, unreadable} — trend-check computes roundsRead from .length on that, so 'no history' and 'could not read history' are the same reading.

mcp-handlers/serve-render/quay-native-store carry the byte-identical QX-041 fence-aware body while cli/flags.ts:178 still strips every /^#+\s/ line unconditionally — and mcp-handlers' own comment records that this exact desync already happened once (SH-005: 'the mcp-server.ts inline copy was not updated by QX-041'), so flags.ts is a third unsynced copy of the same fix.

runner-concurrency.ts exists as the dedicated host-parallelism/suite-slot module and full-suite-runner imports it, but pre-verified-round-record carries its own byte-identical hostParallelism (its comment even says 'the same read-host expression as full-suite-runner.hostParallelism') and its own effectiveParallelism, so the verification-round ledger can report a number no other component agrees with.

tick-core-static-check uses execFileSync with timeout:5_000 and normalises separators; threshold-scope-check uses spawnSync with NO timeout and no separator normalisation, so the scope checker can hang indefinitely on a wedged git where the mandatory tick-core check cannot, and their gitignore exemption sets can differ.

The exported driver-runtime version returns null on an unresolvable sibling (its docstring explicitly forbids falling back to a workspace-root path because ENOENT gets read as 'ran, no data'), while worker-driver's private same-named copy FABRICATES a path — reintroducing exactly the fallback the exported version's docstring forbids — and omits the 'node'/--no-warnings prefix and the .sh branch.

Two paths in, opposite order ((target,base) vs (base,p)) and different equality case (startsWith(base+sep) returns true when equal; path.relative with rel!=='' returns false when equal), so a call routed to the wrong one is not a type error and silently inverts containment — and the exported one is fan-in-materialize's, the likelier import target.

Reversed parameter order ((p,glob) vs (pattern,rel)) AND different matching: one compiles an anchored regex where * does not cross a path separator and ** does, the other special-cases '**', '**/' and trailing '/' and maps * to .* which DOES cross separators, so src/*.ts matches different sets under the two and swapped arguments fail silently.

Three names, four implementations, three incompatible failure contracts: two byte-identical 'git' pairs, gitOut THROWS on failure in landing-target-check but returns null with an extra trim param in store-commit, and runGit returns a normalised {ok,out} object via spawnSync in one file but string|null via execFileSync in the other.

Same name and both exported as a content identity / cache key, but one hashes TEXT with sha1 and the other hashes a FILE PATH with sha256 — a caller swapping them gets a silently wrong cache key with the 40-vs-64-char hex length as the only tell.

TWO names carrying THREE semantics — one drops the quoted span and honours backslash escapes, one drops only the quote characters and KEEPS the content, one replaces the span with the bare quote pair — and registry-bare-filename-scan.ts's in-file comment asserts '(与 runtime-usage-inventory.ts 同语义)' which is FALSE as written; the divergence matters because split(/\s+/) tokenization differs depending on whether the boundary marker survives.

ac61's comment claims it 'mirrors retired-clause-check.norm' but does not: retired-clause's inserts two extra passes that strip '#' and '//' comment prefixes, so (executed) the content '# foo\n# bar' normalises to keep '# foo # bar' under ac61 and 'foo bar' under retired-clause, making the marker 'foo bar' FALSE under one hasMarker and TRUE under the other.

Two bodies under two names: the 81-char pair wraps readFileSync in try/catch returning '', the 98-char pair uses existsSync-then-read with NO try/catch so anything passing existsSync but failing the read (EISDIR, EACCES, dangling symlink, or the TOCTOU window between the syscalls) THROWS where the other reads as 'marker absent'.

Same sentinel (.quay/config.yml) but three resolvers: workflow-event-schema walks 10 levels from its OWN script dir yet its execSync fallback runs in process.cwd() so it can return a DIFFERENT repo's root than it walked from, carrier-dirs takes an explicit startDir with no depth cap and returns null, and repo-root.ts uses a third marker set — and repo-root.ts's header records that findRepoRoot(14)+findWorkspaceRoot(4) were already meant to be unified to one.

meta-store.ts and goal-store.ts carry a byte-identical depth-12 '.git' upward walk, and two more copies exist at depth 12 anchored on cwd and depth 6 anchored on __dirname — none of the four routes through plugin/scripts/repo-root.ts, which exists as the single source of truth for root resolution.

Not one helper under two names: build-evidence-manifest takes (workspaceRoot, milestoneId) and hard-codes the boundary literal, workflow-journal takes (milestoneId, cwd) — arguments 1 and 2 swapped — and delegates to the bash resolver, so a caller mixing the two signatures silently passes a path where an id is expected.

rationale: Byte-identical requestStop one-liners and wakeResolve-augmented sleep bodies redefined in all three resident-loop drivers, which could import the existing driver-shared.ts instead.

One shared atomic helper exists and several callers delegate to it, but ci-runs-collect.ts and driver-anchor.ts re-implement tmp+rename inline while meta-driver.ts writes non-atomically — the atomic/non-atomic split the shared helper exists to close is only partly closed.
The identical try{JSON.parse(readFileSync)}catch{return null} idiom is copy-pasted in three files, each sitting beside a writeJsonAtomic call that is already shared.
Four handlers share the identical parseVerbless to guard to withProvider to resolveGateLogPath to withGuardedErrors to run* pipeline, differing only by the run fn and verb literal.
Byte-identical anchor-tag builder differing only by the route literal, repeated across six serve-* modules; a single entityLink(route,id) collapses all copies.

String and finite-number coercion closures re-declared per function scope six-plus times; serve-binding.ts:77 asNonEmptyString is the same idiom but is not exported, and a weaker variant drops the guard.
The HH:MM formatter and the time-to-x-pixel mapper are re-declared inside each of three SVG render functions; bodies are byte-identical and close over only window/plot params.

repo-root.ts is the canonical unified resolver, but independent upward-walkers survive in workflow-event-schema.mjs (no import-free carve-out documents it) and a byte-identical it0 pair; both existing ratchets miss them by scan face.

Character-identical path-sanitizer duplicated across two files of the same lease-path family; comments claim verbatim reuse but each holds a private copy that can silently diverge on the traversal guard.
Both resolve the same .quay/prepare-leases/<seg>.json; prep factors the dir via leaseDir() while proposal inlines the literal, so the same path contract has two owners.
The identical Atomics.wait(SharedArrayBuffer) synchronous-sleep primitive is redefined in two files despite being a generic utility.
Structurally identical exists/record/corrupt ENOENT-then-JSON readers differing only in the path-getter call; one _readRecordAt(p) collapses both.
Two byte-identical trim/lowercase closure literals in the same file for duplicate owner+reason detection, hoistable to one module-scope helper.

A canonical walkFiles in fs-walk.ts (imported by 21 files, documented as replacing hand-rolled walkers) coexists with twelve local recursive walk closures that re-implement readdir/prune/include; most could be walkFiles calls with prune/include options.
Character-identical prefix-lookup bodies differing only by the default table and an unused element field name; a single prefix-lookup helper serves both.
The object-guarded single-field projection idiom is copy-pasted per field (mfi twice, plus shortCircuit and failReason); one fieldOf(outcome,key) covers all.
Byte-identical CLI fail closure differing only in the printed script prefix; both files already import gate-script-base.ts, the natural home for a shared cliFail.
Two closures in the same file build the same failure object differing only by the activated/revoked discriminator field; one base factory plus spread removes a copy.
The same git merge-base --is-ancestor predicate (false on any git error) implemented twice with different plumbing; a shared git-util would single-source it.
The whenStatus action-button filter predicate is copy-pasted into the CLI and MCP surfaces, with the MCP comment explicitly stating it mirrors quay action list.

Bodies differ only in one semantically-equal identifier; the TS copy names the .mjs as its source and the .mjs already imports a sibling .mjs, so the import-free carve-out is only partial justification.

The settle-once promise latch (if settled return; settled=true; cleanup; resolve) recurs across drivers differing only in resolve payload and cleanup; only the 3-line guard is shareable and it crosses the plugin/packages boundary, so extraction is marginal.

quay-native's findRepoRoot is a deliberate product-layer impl (string|null, .quay/config.yml marker only, no git fallback) that cannot import the plugin's repo-root.ts across the package boundary; same name, different contract.
Two genuinely different glob expanders: suite-bucket-select walks one shallow glob segment mirroring scripts/test.sh, while expandGlobs matches full globs against a precomputed walkFiles list.

Different signatures and data sources building on the shared allDepsDone; ready-pool delegates to the three-value depsReadinessFor while slot-refill is an independent boolean over metaById, so this is by-design divergence.
Each parseArgs is a bespoke per-script flag parser with a different flag set; only the name collides, and the generic flagValue extraction already lives in gate-script-base.ts.
